summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of fibrosing mesenteritis and recurrent partial small bowel obstructions, was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. Imaging showed persistent unconnected tubing in the small bowel with new wall thickening, likely contributing to functional obstruction. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and symptom control. Her G-tube was successfully replaced as planned. She gradually advanced to a full liquid diet, tolerated clamping of the G-tube, and showed improvement in symptoms. She was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue full liquids, monitor phosphate levels with TUMS when consuming Ensure, and follow up with gastroenterology before advancing to solids.
